evidence: Clicking API filter reduced list to 5 API docs; clicking All restored all 19 documents.
Selecting "REST API Design Guidelines" shows title, description, module/date/version (API, 2024-01-15, v2.3.0), 3 content sections, and 4 related documents.

Clicking expanded "REST Principles" header collapsed it: chevron lost rotate-180 class, paragraph body removed, reference links replaced with disabled placeholders (cursor-not-allowed, title 'Expand section to access link').
Expanded sections show chevron with 'rotate-180' class; collapsed sections show chevron without rotation. State consistently matches visible body/links.
Re-clicking collapsed "REST Principles" header restored rotate-180 chevron, the paragraph body, and the active reference link buttons (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards).
From expanded "Endpoint Naming Conventions" section, clicking the active "HTTP Methods Guide" reference link navigated the document view to the "HTTP Methods Guide" document.

Clicking "HTTP Methods Guide" link while section collapsed kept document on REST API Design Guidelines and showed toast "Please expand the section to access links". After expanding, clicking the same link navigated to the HTTP Methods Guide document.
Parsed source data (19 documents): no document's id appears in its own section links (docId) or its own relatedDocs array.
Clicking a graph node added a pulsing glow ring and thicker stroke (selection indicator) vs unselected nodes. Zoom In changed 100%→120% (visible % label). Reset View restored 100%.

Graph shows 19 nodes (one per document) and 19 edges matching relatedDocs/section-link relationships from source data. Reset View sets transform to translate(0,0) scale(1) at 100%, bringing the full graph into view.

19 documents produced 19 graph nodes; each node's stroke/fill color (hsl) matches its module's legend color (API cyan, Auth purple, Data green, UI orange, Core red/pink); 19 unique connections drawn matching related-document data with no self-loops.

issue: Graph node click does not open document view without a tab change
actual: Clicking a node in the Knowledge Graph (e.g. "REST API Design Guidelines") only updates the selected-document state and shows a selection glow on the node; the main panel stays on the Knowledge Graph view (activeTab remains 'graph', confirmed in Index.tsx source where DocumentViewer is only rendered when activeTab is 'documents' or 'favorites'). The user must manually click the "Documents" tab to see the document content, which contradicts the requirement to open the document view "without requiring a separate tab change."
evidence: Index.tsx: activeTab is local useState, only changed by nav tab buttons; KnowledgeGraph's handleNodeClick only calls setSelectedDocumentId/expandSection, never setActiveTab. UI confirmed: after clicking node, nav still highlighted "Knowledge Graph" and no document panel appeared until manually switching to Documents tab.
App provides Documents, Knowledge Graph, and Favorites nav buttons; clicking each successfully switches active view and highlights the correct tab.

After selecting REST API Design Guidelines and expanding two sections, switching Documents→Favorites→Graph kept the same document selected with same section expand states. Separately, zooming Knowledge Graph to 140% and switching to Documents and back preserved 140% zoom.

issue: Favorites list incorrectly filtered by Documents-tab module filter
actual: Favorited "REST API Design Guidelines" (API module) and "JWT Authentication" (Authentication module); nav badge correctly showed "Favorites 2" in real time, and favorite markers survived Documents-tab module filtering/sorting. However, after setting the Documents-tab module filter to "DATA" and switching to the Favorites tab, the Favorites sidebar list showed the empty state ("No favorites yet" / "Star documents to add them to your favorites") even though nav badge still read "Favorites 2" and the DocumentViewer panel still showed "REST API Design Guidelines" with an active "Remove from favorites" state. localStorage (tech-docs-storage) confirmed state.selectedModule = "data" is a single shared filter applied to both Documents and Favorites lists, causing favorited documents outside that module to be hidden from the Favorites view. This violates the requirement that the Favorites view expose every favorited document regardless of a module filter used in Documents.
evidence: document.querySelectorAll('main h3') on Favorites tab (with selectedModule=data) returned ["No favorites yet", ...]; localStorage state.selectedModule === "data" while both favorited docs belong to other modules.

Typing a nonsense search query ("zzzznonexistentquery12345") into the Documents search box replaced the document list with an empty-state message: heading "No documents found" and text "Try adjusting your search or filter criteria". Clearing the search input restored the full list (19 documents visible again via querySelectorAll on document card headings).
